name: Air Fryer Char Siu Pork with Rice and Greens

components.name: Char Siu Pork

ingredients.name: Raw pork shoulder, cut into large thick strips
Hot water for humidifying fryer and basting

steps: Mix sugar, salt, five spice, pepper, sesame oil, Shaoxing wine, soy, hoisin, molasses and garlic. Reserve a small portion of marinade BEFORE it touches pork for safe basting.
Cover pork strips in the remaining marinade and refrigerate a minimum of eight hours, preferably overnight.

Cook a few thick pork strips at a time in an air fryer around 190 C, using a small amount of hot water beneath the rack if your model permits it and checking your appliance instructions. Brush with reserved clean basting liquid.
Turn and baste every 5-6 minutes; internal temperature must reach at least 63 C and rest three minutes for whole cuts. Larger or fatty pieces may need longer for tenderness.
Cool quickly, freeze surplus cooked char siu and rice promptly. Never recommend leaving raw marinating pork out on the counter for hours.

components.name: Jasmine Rice & Greens

ingredients.name: Raw choy sum, bok choy or broccoli

steps: Cook jasmine rice and steam or blanch greens separately. Rest and slice char siu, then portion into eight rice bowls with greens.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Source char siu technique; complete meal adds measured rice and greens. Source recipe provides 8 servings pork alone.
Planning: Overnight marination; small air fryer may require 4+ batches. Original source also uses wine and sugar. Alcohol-free adaptation requires separate approval.
Freezer: cooked char siu and rice freeze well; greens may soften
Dietary: NON-HALAL: CONTAINS PORK and Shaoxing cooking wine/alcohol; soy, sesame, wheat possible.
Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge (≤4°C); refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers, freeze portions for later in the week, and reheat to at least 74°C.
Alcohol-free swap: Shaoxing wine → the same amount of low-sodium chicken stock (or 2 parts unsweetened white grape juice to 1 part rice vinegar).
